about: Every change made to the base witness (W1), and every place where the second witness (W2) differs from it in letters after the spelling equivalences of scripts/rudram/collate.py. check.py proves that text.json equals W1 with exactly these corrections applied, and that the collation still yields exactly these differences.

corrections.reason: W1 runs च and मे together and omits the svarita on च. Every other ‘X च मे’ of the Chamakam is spaced in W1, and W2 marks the svarita on this च (वे॒हच् च् अ॑मेऽ — its own spacing is broken here, the accent is not).
The anunāsika sign is on the wrong v: kalpatām + vyānaḥ is written v̐ + vy, as W1 itself writes कल्पताव्ँ॒वाग्य॒ज्ञेन॑ in the same line. W2: कल्पताम् व्या॒नो.

The anunāsika sign is on the wrong syllable: kalpatām + yajñaḥ is y̐ + ya, as W1 writes श्रोत्रय्ँ॑ य॒ज्ञेन॑ (same unit) and पृ॑थि॒व्याय्ँये॑ (Namakam 11). W2: कल्पताम् य॒ज्ञो. The anudātta stays on य, the syllable before the udātta ज्ञो.

variants.note: W1 writes the doubled bh of the Taittirīya recitation (परि॑ ब्भुज); W2 a single bh. The word is bhuja either way.
W2 एषुधिमते. The stem is iṣudhi- ‘quiver’ (इ॑षु॒धिः, Namakam 1.15; चेषुधि॒मते॑, Namakam 7). Abhinava Śaṅkara’s printed text: नमो निषङ्गिण इषुधिमते तस्कराणां पतये नमः.
W2 ञक्त-. naktam ‘by night’ + carat-; ñ cannot open the word.
W2 आहनव्याय. Sāyaṇa: आहननं … तत्र … उत्पन्न आहनन्यः; Abhinava Śaṅkara’s text: नमो दुन्दुभ्याय चाहनन्याय च.
W2 अवार्त्याय. Abhinava Śaṅkara: नमः पार्याय चावार्याय च; अवारम् … तत्र भवः अवार्यः (the near bank, against pāra the far bank).
W2 आलाट्याय. Sāyaṇa: कर्मफलमत्तीत्यलादो जीवः (alāda, ‘one who eats the fruit of action’); Abhinava Śaṅkara: चालाद्याय, अलादः — जीवः, तत्र भवः अलाद्यः.
W2 निवेष्य्याय. Sāyaṇa: निवेष्पं नीहारजलं तत्र भवो निवेष्प्यः; Abhinava Śaṅkara: निवेष्प्याय.
W2 सहस्रधाः. sahasradhā is an adverb, ‘in a thousand ways’ (Sāyaṇa: सहस्रधा सहस्रप्रकाराः); Abhinava Śaṅkara: सहस्राणि सहस्रधा बाहुवोस्तव हेतयः.
W1 doubles the n of asmin before the vowel of anāturam (the doubling of a final n after a short vowel before a vowel), across the pañcāśat mark; W2 writes a single n. Same words.
W2 प्रातीचीः. pratīcī ‘the west’, beside prācī, dakṣiṇā, udīcī; Abhinava Śaṅkara: दश प्रतीची(र्).
W2 भामस् च: visarga before c can only be ś. Sāyaṇa: मन्युभामाशब्दौ.
W2 शपीति. Sāyaṇa: सपीतिः सहपानम्, beside सग्धिः सह भोजनम्.
W2 अक्षिष्टपच्य. The pair is kṛṣṭapacya / akṛṣṭapacya, ‘ripening in ploughed / unploughed land’.
W2 ends a line on मे and opens the next with अ॒श्विनौ॑, so it spells the elided a. Not a reading.
As C6.3: W2’s line division.
W2 महेन्द्र. The cup is the Māhendra graha, the vṛddhi derivative ‘belonging to the great Indra’, as with every other graha in the list (aindravāyava, maitrāvaruṇa, āśvina, vaiśvadeva …).
W2 पचन्ताः. Sāyaṇa: पचताः शामित्रादयः.
W2 ends a line on मे and leaves its e unchanged before the vowel of the next; W1 writes the sandhi (म उ॒क्षा), as W2 itself does inside a line (म॒ इन्द्र॑श्च).
W2 एकत्रिँश्च्च: a letter is missing. ekatriṃśat ‘thirty-one’ in the series of odd numbers.
W1 writes ñ after ś (श्ञ), the South Indian Taittirīya spelling; W2 श्न. The word is the same (vyaśniya).

svara.note: The svara layer is W1’s. Where W2’s marks differ on an aligned syllable the unit is flagged ‘svara under review’ on its page; no mark is changed on the strength of one witness against the other, except where W1 has dropped a mark that W2 has and the pattern requires (C10.3).
